examples: Near-synonyms: actually, at bottom, at heart, basically, fundamentally, characteristically, centrally, substantially; see also Thesaurus:fundamentally
The beaver is a social creature, not just occasionally but essentially.

quotes.text: A thin, crunchy lemon and thyme rosti was essentially the pimped-up aesthetic of the Kettle chip. That's OK. I like Kettle chips.

quotes.text: A doorknob of whatever roundish shape is effectively a continuum of levers, with the axis of the latching mechanism—known as the spindle—being the fulcrum about which the turning takes place. Applying a force tangential to the knob is essentially equivalent to applying one perpendicular to a radial line defining the lever.

subsenses.definition: (by extension) In essence: in most ways that matter; in all ways that matter.
examples: A: So you're saying, in other words, that he's greedy? B: Essentially, yes, that's what I'm saying.
